language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hello, I am Tim.
Hello, My name is Joe. Meet my friend, Tim. Today, we're exploring the lost city of Atlantis.
Hey Tim, do you see that boat above us? I wonder what makes it move from one end of the sea to the other.

The movement of a boat is called motion. Motion is the change of the position or location of any object. Motion needs a force to cause the change in position. For example, the oars in a boat are used to make a the force that moves the boat forward.
That's interesting! Can you tell me more about motion?
Sure, let me ask you a question. If you want to reach an island in minimum time, what would you prefer: a motor boat or a rowing boat?
A motor boat, of course. It's way faster!
That's correct! A motor boat has a lot more speed compared to a rowing boat. Speed describes motion. Let's see if we can practice with this a bit more.

Look at these small pillars on the floor. They are very old and have been broken off. It's easy to roll them over the floor.

Look at these rocks, we can't roll them easily over the floor. Tim explained to me it's because of friction. Friction is a force between two objects that are in contact. Since the pillar is round and smooth, there isn't as much friction between the pillar and the floor compared to the friction between the rock and the floor.
Look at the rock. It's surface isn't smooth at all and it's also not in a complete round shape. You need more push or pull force to move the rock.

Look at the ball. I'm trying to throw it in the air, but it doesn't stay there. It keeps falling down. Do you know why this happens?

Tim told me this is because of gravity. Gravity is a force determined by the attraction between two objects. The earth uses gravitational force and that's why it pulls the ball back towards the earth once I throw it in the air.
Look at these objects. Can you help me determine what the gravitational force is for these objects?

helperSimple.text: Look at these objects. Gravitational force is determined by the mass of the object. The more mass the object has, the more gravitational force it has. Can you drag the items to the correct box?
